title: Next-month U.S. payroll employment growth versus prior BTOS AI adoption
analysis: exploratory predefined split for small-panel forecasting, not causal inference
primary_metric: RMSE of one-month percentage change in BLS CES seasonally adjusted payroll employee counts
mapping_rule: Use full BTOS collection END calendar month c as origin month. Latest BLS predictor value = c-1 (last generally released month); outcome = 100*(CES[c+1]/CES[c]-1), one-month growth in subsequent calendar month. No Oct 2026 CES (not yet released). For wave 106 ending August 9, forecast September growth.
baseline_features: last published BLS one-month payroll growth to end-month c-1
BTOS firm revenue increase minus decrease percentage shares at survey wave

models.name: M2_AIchange
features: change in BTOS AI % from previous four-week wave

metrics: median and 95% spread of sector resampling of M0-M1 fixed-prediction RMSE difference
scientific_limitations: sector-level observational association, no causal identification; AI use potentially endogenous
CES and BTOS cover different employer/workforce concepts (payroll jobs vs percentage responding firms)
manufacturing and retail broad NAICS groups require equivalence checks
BTOS questionnaires changed in November 2025; no comparably long post-break series
10 purposefully selected industries not probability sample; high within-sector dependence
original CES values are as-of Oct 17 2026, preliminary for Aug/Sep 2026 and subject to revisions
one-month outcome, not 6-12 month structural transformation; longer lags too thin for strong claims
no estimating task reinstatement rho or changing pinned US macro model
